title: Genetic disruption of leucine rich repeat transmembrane protein 4 like 1 induces a pro-social behavioural phenotype in zebrafish
authors: Hillman C; Petracco G; Fontana BD; Scaia MF; Dalla-Vecchia E; Wetton JH; Norton WH; Parker M; Reichmann F
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过斑马鱼基因敲除和转录组分析探讨LRRTM4类似蛋白对社会行为的影响，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract:
Background

Social behaviour encompasses the wide range of interactions that occur between members of the same species. In humans, disruptions in social behaviour are characteristic of many neuropsychiatric disorders, where both genetic risk factors and synaptic dysfunctions can contribute to the phenotype. Among the genes implicated in synaptic regulation, the synaptic adhesion protein leucine-rich repeat transmembrane protein 4 (LRRTM4) has been identified as a key player in maintaining synaptic function and neuronal circuit integrity. Despite its established role in the nervous system, the potential involvement of LRRTM4 in modulating social behaviour and its contribution to social deficits has yet to be explored.

Methods

In the current study, we used zebrafish to study how genetic deletion of lrrtm4l1 , a zebrafish orthologue of LRRTM4 , affects sociality. For this, the social behaviour of homozygous lrrtm4l1 knockout (KO) zebrafish was analysed in multiple behavioural assays and the brain transcriptome of mutant animals was investigated by RNAseq.

Results

KO zebrafish displayed a pro-social phenotype in multiple behavioural assays. Groups of lrrtm4l1 KO zebrafish formed more cohesive shoals and KO individuals spent more time in the vicinity of conspecifics during a social interaction test. They were also less aggressive and in contrast to wild-type zebrafish did not differentiate in their interactions with known and unknown groups of fish. Neurotranscriptomic analysis revealed 560 differentially expressed genes including changes in glutamatergic neurotransmitter signalling, tryptophan- kynurenine metabolism and synaptic plasticity.

Conclusion

These findings suggest that lrrtm4l1 is an important regulator of social behaviour in zebrafish. In a translational perspective, LRRTM4 is a promising potential therapeutic target that warrants further investigation in the framework of neuropsychiatric conditions characterized by major social impairments.
abstract_zh:
背景

社会行为涵盖同一物种成员之间发生的广泛互动。在人类中，社会行为的紊乱是许多神经精神疾病的特征，其中遗传风险因素和突触功能障碍均可能导致该表型。在与突触调控相关的基因中，突触粘附蛋白富亮氨酸重复跨膜蛋白4（LRRTM4）已被确定为维持突触功能和神经回路完整性的关键角色。尽管其在神经系统中的作用已确立，但LRRTM4在调节社会行为中的潜在参与及其对社会缺陷的贡献尚未被探索。

方法

在本研究中，我们使用斑马鱼来研究lrrtm4l1（LRRTM4的斑马鱼直系同源物）的基因缺失如何影响社会性。为此，在多种行为学实验中分析了纯合lrrtm4l1敲除（KO）斑马鱼的社会行为，并通过RNAseq研究了突变动物的大脑转录组。

结果

KO斑马鱼在多种行为学实验中表现出亲社会表型。lrrtm4l1 KO斑马鱼群体形成更紧密的鱼群，且KO个体在社会互动测试中花更多时间靠近同种个体。它们也较少具有攻击性，并且与野生型斑马鱼相比，在与已知和未知鱼群的互动中没有表现出差异。神经转录组分析揭示了560个差异表达基因，包括谷氨酸能神经递质信号传导、色氨酸-犬尿氨酸代谢和突触可塑性的变化。

结论

这些发现表明，lrrtm4l1是斑马鱼社会行为的重要调节因子。从转化医学的角度来看，LRRTM4是一个有前景的潜在治疗靶点，值得在以严重社会障碍为特征的神经精神疾病框架中进一步研究。
